title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 3.8.1 Parable of the lost coin

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

A parable is a story Jesus told to teach a truth about God. In Luke 15:8-10 a woman loses one of her ten silver coins, searches until she finds it, and calls her friends to rejoice. Jesus says heaven rejoices in the same way over one sinner who repents. In this sub-strand you will retell the parable and learn about God's love for the sinner.

## Strand 3.0: The Life of Jesus Christ
Sub-strand 3.8.1: Parable of the lost coin
Suggested lessons: 2

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 The Life of Jesus Christ, Sub-strand 3.8.1 Parable of the lost coin
• Luke 15:8-10

PAGE 2: Learning outcomes

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) retell the parable of the lost coin
b) list lessons learnt from the parable of the lost coin
c) recognise God’s love for the sinner and the need to live a righteous life
d) appreciate God’s love and lead upright lives

## Key inquiry questions
1. How does God show love for the sinner?

PAGE 3: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• read Luke 15:8-10 and retell the parable of the lost coin
• role-play the parable of the lost coin
• share lessons learnt from the parable of the lost coin with a friend
• say how God loves them and how to lead a righteous life
• tell why it is important to live a holy life as a Christian
• sing a song about God’s willingness to save the lost

## Core competencies
• Learning to learn: the skill of sharing what they have learnt is exhibited as they share lessons learnt from the parable of the lost coin.
• Imagination and creativity: the skill of coming up with new ideas is exhibited as learners role-play the parable of the lost coin.

## Values
• Love: is nurtured as learners say how God loves them and how to lead a righteous life.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Financial literacy: learners appreciate the value of currency or money as depicted by the woman’s persistence in search for her lost coin.
• Citizenship: desire to help and work for the salvation of the lost persons (sinners) in their society as an extension of good neighbourliness and care for one another in society.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners read and learn new words.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing and role play.

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: The woman and the coin

LESSON 1: THE WOMAN AND THE COIN
================================

## What you will learn
• Retell the parable of the lost coin from Luke 15:8-10.
• List the lessons learnt from the parable.

Curriculum outcomes: a) retell the parable of the lost coin; b) list lessons learnt from the parable of the lost coin

## Introduction
If you lose one coin from the little money you were keeping carefully, you do not shrug and walk away. You look until you find it. Jesus used that kind of search to teach about God.

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: The woman and the coin — Notes 1

## Notes

Read Luke 15:8-10 and retell it in three short movements.

Jesus said, "Suppose a woman has ten silver coins and loses one. Doesn't she light a lamp, sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it? And when she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbours together and says, 'Rejoice with me; I have found my lost coin.' In the same way, I tell you, there is rejoicing in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents."

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: The woman and the coin — The picture

### The picture
She had ten coins. She lost one. She did not say the nine were enough. She lit a lamp so she could see, swept the house so the coin could not hide in the dust, and searched carefully until she found it. Then her joy was too big to keep alone. She called friends and neighbours to rejoice with her.

PAGE 7: Lesson 1: The woman and the coin — Lessons learnt

### Lessons learnt
- One coin mattered. One person matters to God.
- God searches for the sinner the way the woman searched for the coin.
- Repentance is the finding: a sinner turns back to God.
- Heaven rejoices when one sinner repents. The joy is shared, as the woman shared hers.
- We should not despise a person who has done wrong and then turns back.
- What is valuable is worth a careful search. The coin was worth the lamp, the sweeping and the time.

Share these lessons with a friend in your own words. Role-play the lighting of the lamp, the sweeping, the finding, and the call to rejoice. Do not add a second story. This parable stops at the joy of heaven over one sinner who repents.

PAGE 8: Lesson 1: The woman and the coin — Key words

## Key words
• parable — a story Jesus told to teach a truth about God
• sinner — a person who has done wrong against God
• repent — to turn away from sin and turn back to God

PAGE 9: Lesson 1: The woman and the coin — Retell and role-play the search

## Activity: Retell and role-play the search
You will need: Bible, A coin or bottle top, A small brush or cloth

1. Read Luke 15:8-10 and retell the parable of the lost coin.

2. Role-play the woman lighting a lamp, sweeping, finding the coin, and calling friends to rejoice.

3. Share with a friend the lessons learnt from the parable.

4. Sing a song about God's willingness to save the lost.

PAGE 10: Lesson 1: The woman and the coin — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. How many silver coins did the woman have, and what did she lose?

2. What three things did she do to find it?

3. What happens in heaven when one sinner repents?

## Answers to practice

1. She had ten silver coins and lost one.

2. She lit a lamp, swept the house and searched carefully until she found it.

3. There is rejoicing in the presence of the angels of God.

## Summary
• The woman searched carefully until she found her one lost coin.
• She called her friends to rejoice with her.
• Jesus said heaven rejoices in the same way over one sinner who repents.

PAGE 11: Lesson 2: God's love and a righteous life

LESSON 2: GOD'S LOVE AND A RIGHTEOUS LIFE
=========================================

## What you will learn
• Explain how the parable shows God's love for the sinner.
• Choose to live a righteous and upright life.

Curriculum outcomes: c) recognise God’s love for the sinner and the need to live a righteous life; d) appreciate God’s love and lead upright lives

## Introduction
The woman did not search because the coin searched for her. She went after what was lost. Jesus says God rejoices when a sinner repents. That joy shows love.

PAGE 12: Lesson 2: God's love and a righteous life — Notes 1

## Notes

The key question is: How does God show love for the sinner? In this parable He is like the woman who will not rest until the lost coin is found. The rejoicing of the angels shows that heaven wants the sinner home. Love here is not a soft word that leaves people in sin. Love searches, and love rejoices when there is repentance.

PAGE 13: Lesson 2: God's love and a righteous life — A righteous life

### A righteous life
Righteous and upright mean living in a way that is right before God. The parable does not say the lost coin stays lost and everyone is happy. Joy comes when it is found. In the same way, joy comes when a sinner repents. A Christian who has been found should not choose to be lost again.

Ways to lead a righteous life:

- Admit wrong actions and turn from them.
- Tell the truth.
- Obey parents and teachers.
- Forgive instead of taking revenge.
- Keep your body pure.
- Pray and read God's word.
- Help someone else turn back to God by a kind word, not by mockery.

PAGE 14: Lesson 2: God's love and a righteous life — Why holiness matters

### Why holiness matters
A holy life is a life set apart for God. It matters because God loves you and has searched for you. Living carelessly after being found is like dropping the coin into the dust again. Appreciate God's love by thanking Him and by walking uprightly.

You can also care about people who are far from God. Citizenship in this lesson includes a desire to see lost people saved, as neighbours we care for. Pray for them. Invite them to church with a parent's knowledge. Do not insult them. The angels rejoice over one. You can rejoice too, and you can live in a way that shows the love that found you.

PAGE 15: Lesson 2: God's love and a righteous life — Example 1

## Key words
• righteous — living in a way that is right before God
• upright — honest and straight in character
• rejoice — to be full of joy, as heaven is over one sinner who repents

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A boy says, "God only loves people who never do wrong." How does Luke 15:10 answer him?

Working:
1. The verse speaks about a sinner who repents.
2. Heaven rejoices over that one person.
3. The search and the joy show love for the sinner, and repentance is the right response.

Answer: God loves the sinner and rejoices when that sinner repents. Love calls the person to turn back, not to stay in sin.

PAGE 16: Lesson 2: God's love and a righteous life — How God loves and how we live

## Activity: How God loves and how we live
You will need: Bible, Exercise book

1. Say how God loves you, using the parable of the lost coin.

2. Say how a learner can lead a righteous life.

3. Tell why it is important to live a holy life as a Christian.

4. Sing a song about God's willingness to save the lost.

## Practice

1. How does God show love for the sinner in this parable?

2. What must the sinner do for that joy to fit the story?

3. Give two ways to live an upright life.

PAGE 17: Lesson 2: God's love and a righteous life — Answers to practice

## Answers to practice

1. He searches for the lost, like the woman with the coin, and heaven rejoices when one sinner repents.

2. Repent, which means turn away from sin and turn back to God.

3. Any two: admit wrong and turn from it, tell the truth, obey, forgive, keep pure, pray, help others kindly.

## Summary
• God's love searches for the sinner and rejoices over repentance.
• A righteous life turns from sin and obeys God.
• Appreciate that love by living an upright life.

PAGE 18: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. The parable of the lost coin is in...
   A. Luke 15:8-10
   B. Luke 13:18-19
   C. John 3:1-5
   D. Matthew 5:42

2. The woman had...
   A. ten silver coins and lost one
   B. one coin and lost ten
   C. no lamp
   D. a mustard seed only

3. To find the coin she...
   A. lit a lamp, swept the house and searched carefully
   B. went to sleep
   C. asked a king to curse someone
   D. threw the other coins away

4. When she found it she...
   A. hid it and stayed silent
   B. called her friends and neighbours to rejoice
   C. lost it again on purpose
   D. sold her lamp

5. Jesus said there is rejoicing in the presence of the angels over:

6. One lesson from the parable is...
   A. one person does not matter
   B. one sinner who repents brings joy in heaven
   C. searching is a waste of time
   D. friends should not be told good news

7. The coin was worth a careful search. This teaches that:
   A. people are valuable to God
   B. only rich people matter
   C. lost things should be ignored
   D. angels do not care

8. God shows love for the sinner by...
   A. refusing to look for them
   B. seeking them and rejoicing when they repent
   C. celebrating sin
   D. hiding the lamp

9. A righteous life after being found means:
   A. returning to the same sins on purpose
   B. turning from sin and obeying God
   C. mocking people who repent
   D. refusing to pray

10. Why should a Christian live a holy life?

PAGE 19: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. A. Luke 15:8-10
   The class reads Luke 15:8-10.

2. A. ten silver coins and lost one
   Luke 15:8 says she had ten silver coins and lost one.

3. A. lit a lamp, swept the house and searched carefully
   Luke 15:8 lists the lamp, the sweeping and the careful search.

4. B. called her friends and neighbours to rejoice
   Luke 15:9 says she called them to rejoice with her.

5. One sinner who repents.
   Luke 15:10 gives this meaning.

6. B. one sinner who repents brings joy in heaven
   The woman's joy and heaven's joy both turn on one who was lost and is found.

7. A. people are valuable to God
   The search shows the value of the one who is lost.

8. B. seeking them and rejoicing when they repent
   The woman is the picture of that seeking love.

9. B. turning from sin and obeying God
   Repentance leads to an upright life.

10. Because God loves them, heaven rejoices when a sinner repents, and a holy life stays close to that love.
   The parable's joy is over repentance, so the right response is an upright life.

questions.question: To find the coin she...
options: lit a lamp, swept the house and searched carefully
asked a king to curse someone
questions.explanation: Luke 15:8 lists the lamp, the sweeping and the careful search.

questions.question: When she found it she...
options: called her friends and neighbours to rejoice
questions.explanation: Luke 15:9 says she called them to rejoice with her.

questions.question: Jesus said there is rejoicing in the presence of the angels over:
One lesson from the parable is...
options: one sinner who repents brings joy in heaven
searching is a waste of time
friends should not be told good news
questions.explanation: The woman's joy and heaven's joy both turn on one who was lost and is found.

questions.question: The coin was worth a careful search. This teaches that:
questions.explanation: The search shows the value of the one who is lost.

questions.question: God shows love for the sinner by...
options: seeking them and rejoicing when they repent
questions.explanation: The woman is the picture of that seeking love.

questions.question: A righteous life after being found means:
options: returning to the same sins on purpose
turning from sin and obeying God
questions.explanation: Repentance leads to an upright life.

questions.question: Why should a Christian live a holy life?
questions.answer: Because God loves them, heaven rejoices when a sinner repents, and a holy life stays close to that love.
questions.explanation: The parable's joy is over repentance, so the right response is an upright life.
